topic: Existing assets audit: what the System 1 browser fleet should reuse from browser-box, an older local tool checkout and several related repositories

claims.claim: Self-hosted Steel OSS ignores the value of userDataDir. Any truthy userDataDir or persist:true uses the single fixed directory <build>/../../user-data-dir, which is /app/api/user-data-dir in the image.
claims.evidence: steel-browser api/src/services/session.service.ts:180-183 @1131a02; image sha256:7a161b95… /app/api/build/services/session.service.js:89-91. Spike: POST /v1/sessions {persist:true,userDataDir:'/tmp/custom-profile-x'} returned 200, the Steel log shows userDataDir /app/api/user-data-dir, and /tmp/custom-profile-x was never created (RESULTS.md row 1).
claims.why_it_matters: Per-profile isolation cannot come from one Steel instance with many profile paths. It needs one Steel container per awake profile with that profile's volume mounted at the fixed path, or a patched Steel.

claims.claim: OSS Steel's CreateSession schema has no persistProfile/profileId fields. browser-box's steel.create_session sends them, they are silently stripped, and the request still returns 200.
claims.evidence: sessions.schema.ts @1131a02 (only persist and userDataDir); grep of /app/api/build for persistProfile|profileId returns nothing; browser-box gateway/gateway/steel.py:103,105 @4c837a3; spike create with those fields returned 200.
claims.why_it_matters: The box's session persistence holds only within one Steel lifetime. The fleet cannot reuse steel.py's profile fields, and the box's session card slightly overclaims.

claims.claim: One OSS Steel process runs one browser session at a time, through a single activeSession.
claims.evidence: steel-browser api/src/services/session.service.ts:67 'public activeSession: Session' @1131a02; image session.service.js has 20 references to activeSession.
claims.why_it_matters: Fleet density is one Steel container per concurrently awake profile, so RAM per awake profile (≈550 MiB to 1.36 GiB measured) caps concurrency per host.

claims.claim: Recreating a Steel container on an existing profile volume with a stale Chromium SingletonLock makes Steel log a process_singleton launch error, still return HTTP 200 from POST /v1/sessions, and serve a browser without the profile's cookies. Removing Singleton* restores them.
claims.evidence: RESULTS.md rows 6-7 (2026-10-10 03:05-03:07 UTC): the volume still held the cookies; the log says 'The profile appears to be in use by another Chromium process'; after rm Singleton*, the cookies were present.
claims.why_it_matters: 'Still logged in' must be verified after every wake. The infra 200 is not proof. The wrapper must clear locks under a one-container-per-profile lease.

claims.claim: A cookie set about 5 s before Steel release was not persisted; one set 40 s before release was. This was n=1, and release calls browser.close() then process().kill().
claims.evidence: RESULTS.md rows 2-4; image cdp.service.js:382-383 and endSession at :984.
claims.why_it_matters: Releasing a profile immediately after a human login can silently lose the auth the fleet promises to keep.

claims.claim: browser-box's lane lock is host-local: an fcntl flock on a file path, which cannot coordinate across hosts.
claims.why_it_matters: A multi-droplet fleet needs a DB lease. An earlier internal job-claim design exists as a starting point, but it is safe only serially.

claims.claim: An earlier internal job-claim design leases at most one job per browser profile (lease not expired), uses Postgres SKIP LOCKED with a hashed lease token, and holds jobs with uncertain_external_state instead of retrying them.
claims.evidence: An earlier internal job-claim design at a pinned commit (file and line references withheld).
claims.why_it_matters: A ready-made pattern for 'one profile, one writer' and safe handling of uncertain posts and replies at fleet scale.

claims.claim: browser-box's Browser-Use runner is pinned to browser-use 0.13.10 and refuses any other installed version. The shared scratch venv has 0.13.11, so the self-check fails.
claims.evidence: agents/browseruse/runner.py:32 PINNED='0.13.10', :58 version check @4c837a3; running scratch venv python -I runner.py --self-check prints 'browser-use 0.13.11 is installed; the confinement here is written against 0.13.10'.
claims.why_it_matters: Reusing the confinement requires a re-pin and re-validation against the browser-use version the fleet chooses.

claims.claim: Existing code calls TypeSafe System One by direct HTTP POST to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with model 'jev-1.13.0' and typed questions {type:'choice', criteria, instructions}.
claims.evidence: The trial's model client at a pinned commit (file references withheld); jev-automation package.json @typesafe-ai/sdk ^0.6.0 @edcbbae.
claims.why_it_matters: Grounds the System-1 integration in a real call shape, not the Gemini conversation's invented api.typesafe.com/v1/jev/decide. The System-1 dossier should confirm it against live docs.

claims.claim: The System One trial has measured zero live System-One or GLM cases. Its 100/100 offline result used scripted choices with no model calls, and its ≥95% live target is not met.
claims.evidence: The trial's reports at a pinned commit (zero live provider calls; no committed model usage).
claims.why_it_matters: No existing evidence supports 'System 1 powers 90%+ of actions'. It must be measured per procedure.

claims.claim: box-kit's export script archives the whole browser-box repo at a ref into the public box-kit repo, excluding only .claude-plugin, .mcp.json, skills, commands, bench and tests/test_plugin.py.
claims.evidence: github.com/jbellsolutions/box-kit scripts/export.sh @52710179a71620acd493b0a02061d4a88077e090; gh repo view box-kit isPrivate=false.
claims.why_it_matters: A fleet/ subtree merged to browser-box main would be published unless export.sh excludes it.

claims.claim: guard.Guard takes its CDP URL as a constructor parameter. Only the module-level GUARD singleton is bound to the single Steel, so one Guard can be built per awake browser.
claims.evidence: browser-box gateway/gateway/guard.py class Guard.__init__(self, cdp_url=None) and :318 GUARD = Guard() @4c837a3.
claims.why_it_matters: The fleet can reuse the proven in-browser SSRF guard unchanged, by import, per profile.

gaps: Per-profile container lifecycle for OSS Steel: one container per awake profile, a named volume at /app/api/user-data-dir, Singleton* cleanup, a cookie-flush-safe release, and post-release health/recreate
A per-profile 'still logged in' auth probe after every wake (site-specific markers); infra HTTP 200 is not proof
A per-profile identity pin record (proxy endpoint, UA, timezone, viewport, fingerprint seed) applied identically on every wake, with exit-IP drift detection
A cross-host fleet lease service and per-host capacity scheduler (wake/sleep, routines); lock.py is host-local

Integrating System-1 (Jev) decide/verify into Stagehand's observe/act loop, with per-procedure thresholds measured on target sites; no existing measurement of System-1 share or accuracy on social platforms
An engine router (system1-first → Stagehand → Browser-Use → reasoning) with logged reasons and per-procedure measured winners
Social-platform procedures with platform-specific receipts (the post or DM is visible), campaign authorization manifests, per-profile/per-platform rate caps, and reconciliation of uncertain effects
Human re-auth queue and authenticated, time-limited live-viewer brokering per profile (the box only offers devtools over an SSH tunnel)
A fleet-wide spend ledger across TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Browserbase and proxies, with per-profile, per-client and fleet caps
Encrypted at-rest storage and backup for profile volumes (the trial's portability deliberately excludes cookies, so no pattern exists)
Per-container proxy-only egress rules and a per-image shield-check gate
A fleet Hermes plugin/skill and per-profile scoped token issuance (see the hermes-packaging dossier)
Upstream drift watch and self-checks for Stagehand, Browser-Use and the Steel image digest (the watch does not track Stagehand, Steel or anti-detect)
risks: Silent auth loss in OSS Steel: a stale SingletonLock gave HTTP 200 with a logged-out browser; a fast release lost the cookie; release returned 500 twice and left no browser. Each was seen once or twice on arm64 Docker and needs repeating on amd64 droplets
Steel being single-session per process plus ~0.55-1.36 GiB per awake browser means RAM per awake profile, not profile count, limits scale
No measured basis for '90% System 1': 0 live trial cases, and B5 recorded a Jev search grounding miss (0/3)
Prompt injection: DMs and comments are attacker-written and agents act logged in; Browser-Use is the most exposed
No existing asset has tested anti-detection on Steel; an older local tool's matrix covers other products and is partly vendor claims

Policy tension: an earlier internal outbound-email project disclaims fingerprint spoofing and proxy rotation, while the fleet brief seeks anti-detect, proxies and stealth. This needs Justin's explicit position, plus platform-ToS and client-consent framing
Public export leak: box-kit/scripts/export.sh publishes the whole browser-box repo, so fleet/ would leak if merged before export.sh excludes it

Repo visibility mismatch: jev-automation (a public fork), jev-agent-kit, super-saiyan-browser, hermes-workforce-router and box-kit are public, despite the brief calling them private. Never commit client procedures or account handles there
Version drift: browser-use pin 0.13.10 vs scratch 0.13.11; Steel image 2026-09-16 vs source 2026-10-06; jev-1.13.0 pinned in code
Guard DNS is resolved locally while proxied Chromium resolves at the proxy. Effect on detection or geo-consistency is unknown
Profile volumes hold clients' logged-in social accounts, a high-value secret store with no encryption, backup or access design yet
browser-box's session card and steel.py persistProfile slightly overclaim persistence on OSS Steel. This is the box owner's fix, not made here
Another agent's container fleet-spike-antidetect was running on the shared Docker host during this spike; it was left untouched
recommendations: Base Steel persistence on one container per awake profile with a named volume at /app/api/user-data-dir. The wrapper entrypoint removes Singleton* only while the profile's lease is held. Never rely on userDataDir values, persistProfile or profileId
After every wake, run a site-specific logged-in probe before any work. On failure, move the profile to needs_reauth and stop; do not attempt a login

Never release a profile within 30-40 s of a login or auth change until a better flush mechanism is proven. Test Steel sessionContext export and inject as a second copy, and a fixed --hostname per profile as a lock alternative
Pin the Steel image by digest (sha256:7a161b95… or a newer reviewed one) and re-run this persistence spike plus the 18-attack shield-check on an amd64 droplet before relying on it
Import browser-box gateway.security and gateway.guard.Guard into fleet code (one Guard per awake browser) rather than copying them, and run tests/scope_vectors.json in the fleet suite
Build the fleet lease and scheduler on a DB-enforced one-lease-per-profile rule (hashed token, uncertain means held), with lock.py's flock only as a same-host second guard

Build procedures, receipts and release rules on the pattern of an earlier internal trial: digest-pinned, adapters declare authority and a verifier, intent journaled before the effect, never replay, three accepted outcomes before release, rollback per procedure

Lift jev-automation core/{decide,verify,elements,scope}.ts into the Stagehand worker as the System-1 layer, and measure per-procedure thresholds and the System-1 share on held-out cases before claiming any percentage

Replace per-action post confirmation with immutable campaign authorization manifests (an earlier internal approval-manifest pattern) plus independent receipts, and keep per-action human confirmation outside the manifest
Before any merge of fleet/ to browser-box main, add --exclude='fleet' to box-kit/scripts/export.sh, or explicitly decide what may be public
Ask the browser-box owner to correct steel.py's persistProfile/profileId and the session card's persistence wording. Do not change it from the fleet branch
Re-pin the Browser-Use runner to the version the browser-use dossier chooses and re-run runner.py --self-check; it currently refuses 0.13.11
Extend the internal drift-watch pipeline's queries with Stagehand, steel-browser, Browserbase, DICloak and anti-detect so upstream changes trigger re-validation
Ask Justin to state the fleet's position on fingerprint spoofing, proxy rotation and stealth, given that earlier internal project's disclaimer, before the fleet charter is finalized
Tell the orchestrator that several repos the brief calls private are public (jev-automation, jev-agent-kit, super-saiyan-browser, hermes-workforce-router, box-kit)

Treat the older local tool checkout as now superseded by another repo. Use only its publishing-safety taxonomy, verifier checklist, ledger and proxy-tier notes; do not use its Steel or Browser-Use specialist skills (Cloud-targeted) or its anti-detection conclusions
